strengths: The proposed activation-wise signature is an interesting diagnostic contribution. Combining affine Gaussian optimal transport with a normalized distributional discrepancy provides a common framework for comparing activation behavior across architectures. The recovery result for positive-definite linear transformations gives the construction a useful, restricted theoretical foundation.

The empirical survey is substantial: 36 models spanning convolutional, residual, NAS-based, and transformer architectures, evaluated using the 50,000-image ImageNet validation set. The raw signatures and architectural comparisons reveal informative patterns beyond benchmark accuracy.

The controlled comparison between plain and residual ResNet20 in Figure 7 is particularly valuable. It links a concrete architectural intervention to higher affinity scores after residual connections, supporting the signature's usefulness for inspecting activation behavior.

The supplementary checks cover batch size, nine training seeds for VGG16, alternative input datasets, and supervised/self-supervised checkpoints. These checks, together with supplementary proofs and a public code link, support scrutiny and potential reuse. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-mybjde80/call-21474a03156047dd9e8ad7934531168f/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}
weaknesses: The central interpretation as a theoretically sound measure of functional nonlinearity is not established. Equation 5 compares marginal distributions and can completely miss nonlinear input-output dependence. For example, if X is uniform on [-1,1] and σ(x)=2|x|-1, then σ(X) has exactly the same distribution as X. Consequently, T_aff is the identity and the affinity score is 1, although σ is nonlinear. Theorem 3.3 supplies a sufficient condition under restricted linear transformations, not the claimed converse that equality occurs only for linear functions. This materially limits the main contribution's advertised guarantee.

Activation signatures do not establish the nonlinearity or expressive power of complete networks. The plotted ViT signatures measure GELU behavior, while attention's input-dependent operations and layer normalization also contribute nonlinearity. No composition result or direct validation connects these signatures to overall functional complexity. Similarly, a nearly affine post-residual ReLU does not establish that the residual block has learned an identity function. The evidence supports architectural differences in activation behavior more strongly than the broader explanations of transformer capability.

The accuracy analysis in Figure 6 selects the best statistic separately for each small architecture group and evaluates its fit on those same models. For example, the ViT result with R²=0.974 uses only five models. Without held-out evaluation, selection-adjusted uncertainty, or controls for model size and training differences, these results establish exploratory associations rather than reliable predictive value or an explanation of accuracy improvements.

The justification against alternative measures contains consequential errors. A least-squares affine fit with an intercept has in-sample R² in [0,1], so negative unbounded R² is not an inherent disadvantage of an appropriate regression baseline. ReLU's nondifferentiability at zero also does not generally preclude Jacobian-based evaluation, since it is differentiable almost everywhere. Finally, weak Pearson correlations with selected metrics establish difference, not superior validity or useful additional information.

The implemented estimator needs clearer qualification. Appendix C's spatial averaging is not lossless and generally changes the input-output relationship being measured; Figure 9 does not establish its validity across the architectural survey. Covariance shrinkage also changes the exact moment-matching construction. The manuscript does not clearly specify the numerical Wasserstein solver or handling of zero output variance, where Equation 5 is undefined, including entirely inactive ReLUs. These are secondary reproducibility concerns, while the validity and interpretation issues above determine the weak-reject recommendation.
